body:
Advertising that persuades older people to move their shopping and banking online does them more good than harm.

To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Buying second-hand clothes, furniture and electronics is usually a better choice than buying the same items new.

Do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Short videos watched on mobile phones are shortening people's attention spans and making it harder for them to concentrate on longer tasks such as reading a book.

Do you think this is a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Headlines written mainly to attract clicks make it harder for readers to understand events, so news organisations should be judged on accuracy rather than on how many people read their stories.

To what extent do you agree or disagree with this opinion?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Some people believe that anonymity on the internet protects people who speak out against unfair treatment. Others think that people who hide their identity behave more cruelly towards others and should not be allowed to post comments online.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Journalists argue that they must be free to publish anything the public finds interesting. Others believe that the private lives of ordinary people should be protected from media attention, even when the information is true.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Some people think that advertising on billboards, bus shelters and the sides of buses makes towns more lively and interesting. Others feel that it spoils the appearance of public spaces and that people should not be forced to look at it.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Film-makers often accept payment from companies that want their products to appear on screen. Some people argue that this is a sensible way to pay for films and makes stories more realistic, while others feel that it misleads audiences and turns entertainment into advertising.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Many online shops now offer free returns, so customers can order several sizes or colours and send back the items they do not want.

Do you think the advantages of free returns outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Pay-later schemes, which let shoppers receive goods immediately and pay in monthly instalments, are becoming common in online shops.

To what extent do the advantages of pay-later schemes outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Supermarkets and high street shops give customers loyalty cards that collect information about what they buy in return for discounts and points.

Do you think the advantages of loyalty card schemes outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Local newspapers are closing across the world, and many towns no longer have a publication that reports on their council, schools and local businesses.

What are the causes of this?

What can be done to keep local news services alive?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Many apps and online games designed for young children collect personal data about their users, often without the children or their parents understanding what happens to that information.

Why does this happen?

What measures should companies and governments take to protect the privacy of children online?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Many households now pay for so many subscriptions to streaming services, music, apps and online magazines that they lose track of how much money they spend each month.

What are the reasons for this?

What measures could individuals and companies take to deal with this problem?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Most people read online reviews before buying a product, but many reviews are written by sellers or paid for by companies.

Why do many shoppers continue to trust online reviews?

What can shoppers do to check whether a review is genuine?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Many people now have hundreds of online friends, yet they say they feel lonelier than people did before social media existed.

Why do people feel this way?

Are friendships formed online as valuable as friendships built face to face?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Some people choose a digital detox, spending a week or a month without using their smartphones or social media accounts.

Why do people feel the need to do this?

Is a digital detox an effective way to improve well-being?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
